diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, $(\cdot,\cdot)_\omega$ denotes the $L^2$ inner product over $\omega$, and $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_{\omega}$ denotes the duality pairing between $H^{-1/2}(\omega)$ and $H^{1/2}(\omega)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The weak imposition of the flux boundary condition uses γ h^{-1}(u_Γ, v_h·n)_Γu written with the L² inner-product notation (the paper explicitly reserves ⟨·,·⟩_ω for the H^{-1/2}–H^{1/2} duality), but the standing data assumption is only u_Γ ∈ H^{-1/2}(Γ_u). Since v_h·n ∈ L²(Γ_u) is not in H^{1/2}(Γ_u) in general, the pairing cannot be reinterpreted as a duality either, so the discrete right-hand side ℓ_h is undefined for u_Γ ∈ H^{-1/2}(Γ_u) \ L²(Γ_u). The same omitted hypothesis affects the boundary term γ h^{-1}‖(u−u_h)·n‖²_{L²(Γ_u)} inside the ‖·‖_{d,h} norm on the left-hand side of Theorem thm:added-1, and the pairings (v_h·n, p)_Γu used in its consistency step when p ∈ H^t with t ≤ 1/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standing hypothesis u_Γ ∈ L²(Γ_u) (and, for the error analysis, an L²(Γ_u)-trace of p, e.g. t > 1/2), restricting the formulation and Theorem thm:added-1 to that data class; all methods, rates and results are preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete problem (eq:discrete-problem), the functional ℓ_h and the boundary-trace components of the error analysis are well defined only under stronger trace assumptions (u_Γ ∈ L²(Γ_u); L²(Γ_u)-trace of p) than stated; as written they are undefined for part of the paper's declared data class.
issues.title: Flux boundary penalty pairing is undefined for the assumed H^{-1/2} flux data
issues.why_classification: A standard local trace-regularity hypothesis on the boundary data makes every term well defined; the method, rates and advertised scope for the regularity class actually used in the estimates all survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The interpolation estimates for $u$, $\dv{u}$ and $p$, together with the trace inequality for the boundary term in $\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{d},h}$ and Assumption~\ref{as:extensions}, then prove the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed bound includes γ h^{-1}‖(u−u_h)·n‖²_{L²(Γ_u)} = O(h^{2r}). (a) The proof's own route (triangle inequality with w_h = Π_{d,h}u, the cut trace inequality, and ‖∇(u−Πu)‖ ≲ h^{r−1}‖u‖_{H^r}) yields only γ h^{-1}‖(u−Πu)·n‖² ≲ h^{2r−2}‖u‖²_{H^r}, one order below the claim. (b) The claimed rate is also unattainable: ‖(u−u_h)·n‖_{L²(Γ_u)} is bounded below by the best approximation of u·n|_Γu by normal traces of V_h (piecewise P_{k_u} on O(h) pieces), which for u ∈ H^{k_u+1} is generically O(h^{k_u+1/2}); hence for r = k_u+1 the boundary term is ≳ h^{2k_u} = h^{2r−2}, contradicting O(h^{2r}). Only the volume components (flux L², divergence, pressure) are correctly established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Theorem thm:added-1 with the boundary term at its provable rate, e.g. split the estimate into volume terms at h^{2r}, h^{2s}, h^{2t} and γ h^{-1}‖(u−u_h)·n‖²_{L²(Γ_u)} = O(h^{2r−2}), or modify the norm's boundary weight.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:added-1's optimal-order bound is false in its boundary-trace component (by one order in the squared norm); the provable and sharp statement carries γ h^{-1}‖(u−u_h)·n‖² at rate h^{2r−2}. The abstract's claim of optimal-order a priori error estimates remains valid only for the volume components of the ‖·‖_{d,h} norm.
issues.title: Error estimate overclaims the convergence rate of the boundary flux-trace term
issues.why_classification: The statement is false in one norm component by a full order; the repair is a contained weakening (restating or splitting the boundary term's rate) that preserves the optimal volume rates and leaves a recognizably comparable error theorem, but the advertised optimal bound for the full ‖·‖_{d,h} norm must be weakened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $k_u, k_p \in \{0,1,\ldots\}$ be the largest values such that $[\mathbb{P}_{k_u}(T)]^d \subset \V(T)$ and $\mathbb{P}_{k_p}(T) \subset \Q(T)$ for all $T \in \mathcal{T}_h$, respectively.
To reduce the amount of stabilisation, we instead define $\Fstab$ from the aggregated mesh introduced in Section~\ref{sec:geom}.
The corresponding estimate for $\uh$ follows by the same argument, applied component-wise to each component of $\uh$.

issues.failure_explanation: On quadrilaterals, RT_k = Q_{k+1,k}×Q_{k,k+1} has normal-direction polynomial degree k+1, while the penalty only sums normal-derivative jumps up to order k_u = k (by the definition of k_u). The unpenalized top-order modes defeat Assumption (eq:stab-assump-1) for the advocated aggregate-reduced F_stab: for RT_0 on a Cartesian mesh, v = (b x_1, 0) on a cut cell vanishes on the facet shared with its root, so [D_n^j v] = 0 for all j ≤ k_u on the stabilized facets; taking two facet-adjacent cut cells of different aggregates with v = (b x_1,0) and v = (b(2h−x_1),0) (continuous across the unstabilized inter-aggregate facet, zero normal traces elsewhere) gives an H(div)-conforming v_h ∈ V_h with s_h^d(v_h,v_h) = 0, ‖v_h‖_{L²(Ω_h)} ∼ 1 and ‖v_h‖_{L²(Ω)} → 0 as the cut shrinks, violating ‖w_h‖²_{L²(Ω)} + s_h^d(w_h,w_h) ≃ ‖w_h‖²_{L²(Ω_h)}. The proof's final 'same argument, applied component-wise' glosses over this degree mismatch. (On simplices the claim holds, since {v ∈ RT_k(T) : D_n^j v|_F = 0, j ≤ k} = {0} there, and BDM spaces have degree equal to k_u.)

failure_location.quote: The stabilisation terms~\eqref{eq:shface} satisfy Assumption~\ref{as:stabilisation-terms}. {Moreover, the pressure stabilisation satisfies Assumption~\ref{as:pressure-kernel-approx}.}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either extend the derivative range of the flux ghost penalty to the full polynomial degree of V(T) (j ≤ k_u+1 for quadrilateral RT_k) and repeat the routine estimate, or restrict Lemma lem:enhanced-stability-FGP and the face-based stabilisation to element families whose polynomial degree does not exceed k_u (simplicial RT_k, BDM_{k+1}).
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:enhanced-stability-FGP is false for quadrilateral RT_k flux spaces with the aggregate-based F_stab, so Assumption (eq:stab-assump-1) is not satisfied by the face-based stabilisation in that configuration and the stability/error theory (Theorems thm:stability, thm:added-1, thm:pressure-robust-alt) has no verified foundation (and presumably fails) for the face-based method on quadrilateral RT meshes. The simplicial and BDM cases used in the experiments are unaffected.
issues.title: Face-based flux ghost penalty does not control RT_k fluxes on quadrilateral meshes
issues.why_classification: A false lemma with an explicit counterexample for a documented element/mesh combination inside the paper's framework; repairing requires either modifying the stabilisation definition or withdrawing that configuration — contained changes with no impact on the reported experiments, but more than a local notational fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\Gamma_p \neq \emptyset$, the discrete solution $u_h$ satisfies $\dv{u_h} = -\piqst(g)$ on $\Omega_h$.
there exists a constant $c_h \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\dv{u_h} = -\piqst(g) + c_h$ on $\Omega_h$

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own Lemma lem:mass-conservation, div u_h = −π_h^0(g) (up to a constant), and the stabilised projection equals the identity on Q_h only on the kernel of s_h^0 (setting q_h = π_h^0(g)−g in the projection equation shows π_h^0(g) = g forces s_h^0(g,·) = 0). Hence g ∈ div(V_h) (g linear, div RT_1 ⊂ P_1) does not by itself imply exact discrete conservation; a piecewise-linear g with kinks would give div u_h ≠ −g. The machine-precision divergence actually holds because g(x,y) = 2x+2y−3/2 is a single global polynomial, so all jumps [D^j g] vanish and g lies in the stabilisation kernel. The stated 'since' is an invalid inference within the paper's own framework.

failure_location.quote: Since $\dv{\mathbb{RT}_1}\subset \mathbb{P}_1$, we expect machine-precision errors for the divergence with this choice of elements.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the justification: machine precision holds because g is a single global polynomial and hence in the kernel of the pressure stabilisation (π_h^0(g) = g), not because div RT_1 ⊂ P_1.
issues.overall_effect: The stated reason for the expected machine-precision divergence is wrong; the reported observation is correct for the actual data, so no numerical result is invalidated, but the paper attributes exact discrete conservation to the wrong property and would give false expectations for data merely lying in div(V_h).
issues.title: Invalid justification of machine-precision divergence in the rectangle experiment
issues.why_classification: A one-sentence correction of the stated justification; every experimental claim and result stands.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To validate the method, we utilise the following manufactured exact solutions.

issues.failure_explanation: At r = r_int write S = sin(r_int²), C = cos(r_int²). The manufactured solution gives {p} = S + 3/2, [u·n] = ±1/r_int and [p] = ∓1 = η_int{u·n} (condition 1 holds with a consistent jump convention). Condition 2 then forces \hat p = S + 3/2 ∓ 1/(4(4C+3)) = (19 + 12S + 8 sin(2r_int²) + 24C)/(4(4C+3)), whereas the stated formula is (19 r_int² + 12S + 8 sin(2r_int²) + 24 r_int² C)/(4 r_int²(4C+3)); these agree only if r_int² = 1, but r_int = 0.3 (numerically ≈1.63 vs ≈2.53). The sine terms lack the factor r_int² carried by the other terms, so the manufactured solution does not satisfy the stated transmission condition with the stated \hat p, and the discrete problem with this \hat p is inconsistent with the exact solution the experiment claims to validate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct \hat p to the value implied by the manufactured solution and the stated conditions, \hat p = (19 + 12 sin(r_int²) + 8 sin(2r_int²) + 24 cos(r_int²))/(4(4 cos(r_int²)+3)) (equivalently, carry the factor r_int² uniformly through numerator and denominator).
issues.overall_effect: The interface validation experiment as described does not test the stated problem: with the printed \hat p the exact solution violates the transmission condition {p} = \hat p + (η_int/8)[u·n] by an O(1) amount, so the reported convergence to this exact solution cannot follow from the stated data.
issues.title: Interface experiment: stated parameter \hat{p} is inconsistent with the manufactured solution
issues.why_classification: A single forced formula correction (harmonizing the r_int² factors) restores the internal consistency of the experiment; no theorem, method or rate is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In Figure~\ref{fig:interface.example}, we show that we obtain optimal convergence rates and condition-number scaling for the considered element pairs using {the \texttt{FGP} method}.

issues.failure_explanation: Two readings, both defective. (i) Literal reading (V_h, Q_h as defined in Section 3, single-valued on the active mesh): the exact flux jumps across the unfitted interface (u_1·n − u_2·n = 1/r_int ≠ 0), while single-valued discrete fluxes are continuous across Γ_int, so the best-approximation error on the O(h^{-1}) straddling cells is Ω(h^{1/2}) and the reported optimal convergence is unattainable; moreover the terms ([u_h·n],[v_h·n]) and −(\hat p,[v_h·n]) are then identically zero. (ii) Duplicated-space reading (as in the cited interface method, needed for the jump terms to be meaningful): substituting the exact solution and integrating by parts over Ω_1 ∪ Ω_2 leaves the unbalanced residual (7η_int/8)([u·n],[v_h·n])_Γint, because the condition {p} = \hat p + (η_int/8)[u·n] requires the jump-penalty coefficient η_int/8, not η_int. Hence the formulation as stated is either vacuous in its jump terms and suboptimal, or inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the discrete spaces duplicated across Γ_int (as in the cited interface method) and correct the jump-penalty coefficient to η_int/8 (or amend the transmission conditions/right-hand side accordingly), so that the exact solution satisfies the discrete equations.
issues.overall_effect: The interface experiment's discrete formulation (eqs:discrete-interface) does not support the claimed validation: as written it cannot be simultaneously consistent with the stated transmission conditions and capable of the reported optimal convergence rates.
issues.title: Interface discrete formulation is inconsistent or incapable of the reported convergence
issues.why_classification: The described construction is inconsistent under either reading; the repair is contained (respecify the spaces plus one coefficient, with a choice between repairs) and affects only the experiment section, but the claimed validation is unreliable until it is made.

issues.failure_explanation: For the stated flux, div u = −(2γ(r²) + 2r²γ'(r²))/r_int² with γ(r²) = 1 + 2cos(r²) in Ω_1 and 2 + 2cos(r²) in Ω_2, i.e. div u = −(2 + 4cos(r²) − 4r² sin(r²))/r_int² (respectively −(4 + 4cos(r²) − 4r² sin(r²))/r_int²), a transcendental function of r² and not a quadratic polynomial. The claim misstates the structure of the data underlying the divergence-convergence study.

failure_location.quote: Here, note that $\dv{u}$ is quadratic, so we investigate its convergence rate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sentence (e.g. 'div u is smooth but not piecewise polynomial'), leaving the convergence study unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The stated rationale for the divergence convergence study in the interface experiment mischaracterises the data; the observed convergence rates are consistent with the actual (smooth, non-polynomial) divergence, so the numerical conclusions are unaffected, but the stated property is false.
issues.title: False claim that the interface solution's divergence is quadratic
issues.why_classification: A false descriptive claim about the example with a trivial local correction; no estimate, method or numerical result depends on it.
